subject: physiology
title: Growth Hormone Regulation, IGF-1, and Disorders of Growth

steps.tx: Synthesized by abundant somatotrophs comprising fifty percent of the anterior pituitary gland, **human growth hormone**, or somatotropin, is a single-chain polypeptide containing one hundred ninety-one amino acids. It coordinates linear skeletal elongation during childhood and regulates whole-body carbohydrate, lipid, and protein metabolism throughout adult life.
steps.say: Growth hormone is a 191-amino-acid peptide secreted by somatotrophs, driving linear growth and regulating metabolism.

left.title: Direct Metabolic Actions
points: Stimulates hormone-sensitive lipase; promotes adipocyte lipolysis
Inhibits peripheral glucose uptake by downregulating muscle GLUT4
Promotes cellular amino acid uptake and protein synthesis

right.title: Indirect Growth Actions (via IGF-1)
points: Stimulates hepatic synthesis and release of IGF-1 (Somatomedin C)
Drives epiphyseal chondrocyte proliferation and hypertrophy
Stimulates osteoblast differentiation and periosteal bone formation
Promotes systemic visceral organ and soft tissue hyperplasia

steps.tx: Growth hormone secretion is governed by dual hypothalamic control: stimulation by growth hormone-releasing hormone via cyclic AMP, and inhibition by somatostatin via inhibitory Gi pathways. Secretion is episodic and pulsatile, characterized by prominent **nocturnal growth hormone surges** linked to slow-wave Stage 3 and Stage 4 sleep.
steps.say: Hypothalamic GHRH stimulates and somatostatin inhibits growth hormone, which peaks in pulses during deep slow-wave sleep.

nodes.label: Hypothalamic Arcuate Nucleus Emits Pulsatile Burges of GHRH into Portal Blood
GHRH Receptors on Somatotrophs Stimulate Gs -> cAMP Rises -> GH Exocytosis
Periventricular Somatostatin Lowers cAMP, Creating Inter-Pulse Basal Nadirs
Onset of Deep Slow-Wave (N3) Sleep Generates Largest Diurnal Secretory Peak

steps.tx: Potent physiological stimuli that acutely trigger growth hormone release include insulin-induced hypoglycemia, strenuous physical exercise, deep slow-wave sleep, fasting, and intravenous infusion of the amino acid arginine. Conversely, acute postprandial hyperglycemia, elevated free fatty acids, and pharmacological glucocorticoids strongly suppress **somatotroph hormone release**.
steps.say: Hypoglycemia, exercise, and arginine stimulate growth hormone, while hyperglycemia and free fatty acids suppress it.

rows: Hyperglycemia (oral glucose load), elevated free fatty acids
Deep slow-wave sleep (N3), strenuous exercise, stress

steps.tx: Most growth-promoting actions of somatotropin are mediated indirectly by **insulin-like growth factor 1**, historically termed somatomedin C. Synthesized predominantly by the liver in response to growth hormone, circulating IGF-1 circulates tightly bound to insulin-like growth factor binding protein 3, providing a stable twenty-four-hour growth stimulus.
steps.say: Growth hormone stimulates hepatic production of IGF-1, which drives bone growth and circulates bound to IGFBP-3.

left.title: Circulating Growth Hormone (GH)
points: Secreted in short, erratic spikes (half-life ~20 minutes)
Subject to acute fluctuations from stress, meals, exercise
Random single blood draw is of limited diagnostic utility

right.title: Insulin-Like Growth Factor 1 (IGF-1)
points: Synthesized in liver; stable circulating level (half-life ~15 hours)
Bound to ternary complex with IGFBP-3 and acid-labile subunit
Serves as the premier screening biomarker for GH disorders
Exerts insulin-like metabolic effects on peripheral tissues

steps.tx: Persistent hypersecretion of growth hormone by a somatotroph adenoma occurring after epiphyseal plate fusion in adult life causes **clinical acromegaly**. Because long bones can no longer lengthen, excessive periosteal and soft tissue apposition causes enlargement of hands and feet, coarse facial features, prognathism, macroglossia, and visceromegaly.
steps.say: Acromegaly occurs when growth hormone excess develops after epiphyseal fusion, enlarging hands, feet, jaw, and internal organs.

vis.alt: Clinical acromegaly features and craniofacial changes
vis.caption: Prognathism, frontal bossing, acral enlargement, and soft tissue proliferation in acromegaly.

steps.tx: Definitive biochemical diagnosis of acromegaly requires an elevated serum IGF-1 followed by an **oral glucose tolerance test for GH**. In healthy individuals, a seventy-five-gram oral glucose load suppresses growth hormone below one microgram per litre; in acromegaly, autonomous adenomatous somatotrophs fail to suppress growth hormone.
steps.say: The oral glucose tolerance test normally suppresses growth hormone, but autonomous adenomas fail to suppress.

nodes.label: Clinical Suspicion -> Screen with Age- and Sex-Adjusted Serum IGF-1 Level
Administer 75-Gram Oral Glucose Load; Measure Serum GH at 30-Minute Intervals
Normal Response: Serum GH Suppresses to < 1.0 mcg/L (or < 0.4 mcg/L on sensitive assay)
Acromegaly Confirmed: Inadequate Suppression or Paradoxical Rise in Serum GH

steps.tx: When somatotroph adenomas arise during childhood prior to epiphyseal fusion, unrestrained linear chondrogenesis causes **pituitary gigantism**. Affected children exhibit symmetrical accelerated linear growth resulting in extreme statures exceeding two hundred forty centimetres, accompanied by secondary hypogonadotropic hypogonadism due to surrounding gonadotroph compression.
steps.say: Pituitary gigantism arises in childhood before epiphyseal fusion, producing massive symmetrical linear skeletal overgrowth.

vis.alt: Pediatric growth hormone deficiency and skeletal growth plates
vis.caption: Epiphyseal chondrocyte proliferation, growth plate kinetics, and linear growth failure.

steps.tx: Conversely, severe childhood growth failure from end-organ insensitivity to growth hormone produces autosomal recessive **Laron syndrome**. Caused by loss-of-function mutations in the growth hormone receptor, patients present with profound dwarfism, microphallus, and prominent forehead, exhibiting high circulating growth hormone alongside undetectable IGF-1 levels.
steps.say: Laron syndrome is growth hormone receptor insensitivity, causing dwarfism with high growth hormone and low IGF-1.

rows: Pre-pubertal somatotroph adenoma before epiphyseal closure
Post-pubertal somatotroph adenoma after epiphyseal closure
Inactivating mutation of growth hormone receptor (GHR)
Congenital GHRH deficiency or pituitary somatotroph aplasia
Blunted pubertal IGF-1 surge and low receptor density
